articles.headlineTranslated: Are teachers and school staff excluded from measles response measures? | SLIPER BLOG
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Japan highlights that teachers and school staff can be both at risk and transmission sources. Following a sharp measles surge this year, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare issued a May 2026 public guidance on outbreak prevention. The guidance notes measles’ high infectivity and that handwashing or masks alone may not prevent spread; outbreaks in schools have involved staff as well as students. It urges vaccination scrutiny for school personnel: those born before April 2, 2000 may have had only one dose or none; high-risk groups—including healthcare workers and staff at child welfare facilities and schools—should discuss a second MMR dose with their physician, especially when traveling to outbreak countries. Some boards have asked staff to report vaccination status. For support, consult school physicians or local public health centers. See Measles prevention messages, School Measles Guidelines II, and MR vaccine pages.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles outbreak: two-dose vaccination for prevention; those aged 36 and older should be especially cautious — Asahi Shimbun
articles.summary: Measles outbreak in Japan: as of July 26, 2026, 547 cases reported, more than double the 265 cases last year, with ongoing risk despite a recent slowdown. Measles, caused by the measles virus, presents with fever, cough, and rash, and can lead to pneumonia or meningitis; about 1 in 1,000 develop encephalitis, and SSPE can manifest years later. Highly contagious, measles spreads via droplets and airborne transmission and can remain infectious on surfaces or in the air for up to 2 hours; transmission is possible even in moderately sized, enclosed spaces. Incubation averages about 10 days; infectiousness starts one day before fever. Two-dose vaccination is most effective: one dose leaves ~5% without adequate antibodies; two doses confer long-lasting immunity and generally reduce transmission, though breakthrough infections can occur. NIID data from 2025–26 involving ~800 patients show only one secondary case per year among two-dose recipients. The article cautions those aged 36 and older and underscores publicly funded routine vaccination.

articles.headlineTranslated: Measles infections exceed 500 this year, foreign visitors to Japan may have brought the virus... Hope for digitalization of medical information driven by COVID-19 lessons.
articles.summary: Measles infections in Japan surpassed 547 cases by July 8, 2026, second only to 2019’s 744, with Tokyo accounting for about half (264). Genetic analysis indicates that foreign visitors to Japan introduced the virus. Nine of ten patients are under 30, and many have no documented vaccination history. Measles is airborne, with cough, high fever, and rash; about 1 in 1,000 infected may die, and pregnancy loss is a risk. Tokyo leverages the COVID-19–era K-net infectious disease information-sharing system linking 31 public health centers to rapidly share test results, travel histories, and timings, aiding contact tracing and containment. An emergency vaccination program targets those exposed within 72 hours. Logistics upgrades, including a dedicated motorcycle courier network for specimen transport, reduce staff burden. Health experts view these measures as strengthening readiness for future outbreaks.
